# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm Mute, first in the order, and nobody has spoken yet. My manual gives three engraved marks and their wire colors (ᖉ→green, ꔮ→yellow, ꖜ→red). I can't see the bomb and can't talk — my only channel is gestures to Deaf. Deaf can see the plate's mark and the wires' colors but can't hear; Blind can cut but can't see color or print. So the plan: Deaf reports (by voice, which I and Blind can hear) what the engraved mark looks like and the left-to-right layout of the wire colors. I match the mark to my manual, work out which position to cut, and then simply *point* — pointing is the one gesture vocabulary that needs no negotiation — so Deaf can relay "cut that wire" to Blind. For this first turn I ask Deaf, in as self-evident gestures as I can: cooperate, you, the written mark, please — then left-right, asking for the wire row too.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "🫵", "✍", "🙏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "👉"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, I can reach the bomb. Under my fingers: three wire positions, 1, 2, 3; a display I cannot read; a light I cannot see; and a plate engraved with a mark I feel as a circle with an X spanning it, corner to corner, like a crossed ring. The only action I can take is cut, wire 1 to 3. Plan: Deaf cannot hear you, but Deaf can speak, and I hear Deaf one round late. So Deaf describes the visuals aloud, you apply the manual, and you tell me the rule plus the evidence it needs. I will check your instruction against Deaf's own words before cutting. First: what does the manual say about the crossed-circle plate, the display, and the light?
Deaf says: Full bomb read-out. The display shows 0. The light is off. The plate bears one engraved mark, a symbol with no name: I cannot pronounce it and have no shape words for it. Wires, left to right: wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. That is everything printed on it. Mute: I read your handshake, point-at-you, writing-hand, praying-hands as asking for the manual's needs, and your point-left, point-right as asking the order — both answered above. Blind: I read your wave, handshake, raised hand, then 1, 2, 3 as greeting and the three wires; if the raised hand meant stop or wait, acknowledged — nobody cuts anything yet. Proposed code, learn it: thumbs up means yes or correct. Thumbs down means no or wrong. One finger up means 1. Two fingers up means 2. The hand with thumb, index and little finger spread means 3. Point up means wire 2, point left means wire 1, point right means wire 3. Writing hand means the manual. Pointing at you means you. Blind: feel the engraved plate and describe that mark aloud in plain words for Mute to look up. Also say aloud everything else you feel — buttons, switches, screws, the texture of each wire, whether you can feel the light or display. Mute: ask me anything with the code, I will answer in speech. If you need more signs, invent them and I will guess aloud; correct me with thumbs up or thumbs down.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Working through what I now know. Deaf's read-out gives me the bomb's full printed state: display 0, light off, one unnamed engraved mark, wires left to right yellow, green, red. Blind's touch gives me the mark's *shape*, which is the one thing my manual needs: a circle with an X crossing it corner to corner — a crossed ring. Comparing that against the three engravings in my table, the crossed ring is the third one, ꖜ, which the manual sends to the **red** wire. Red is wire 3 in Deaf's left-to-right count, and Deaf has already given me a pointing code: point right means wire 3. My gestures only reach Deaf, and Deaf is the only one of us who can speak, so Deaf must relay my verdict to Blind — Blind has promised to check my instruction against Deaf's own words (wire 3 = red) before cutting. So this turn: confirm Deaf's proposed code with thumbs up, then send manual → crossed mark → wire 3, with a please to pass it on.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🤞", "👉"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, full tactile report for the manual. The engraved mark: a hollow ring, and two straight grooves crossing at its centre to form an X; each of the four arms continues past the rim and ends just outside it. One continuous engraved line — a circle pierced corner to corner with four horns poking out. Look up anything keyed to a mark like that. Rest of the bomb: three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, no bumps, stripes or tags under my fingers, so only Deaf's colours tell them apart: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. A flat display face and a small light dome. Nothing else anywhere I can reach: no buttons, switches, screws or battery pack. Route check: you cannot speak and gestures never reach me, so every rule you find must go to Deaf to be spoken aloud; I hear Deaf one round after Deaf speaks. I cut nothing until Deaf's own mouth gives me the rule. Arming protocol: when I hold a rule, I point at the wire I intend to cut; then I cut only after Deaf has spoken a full round with no stop. If you doubt the plan at any point, get Deaf to say stop.
Deaf says: New code words, both learn them. Fist means zero or nothing. Palm down means light off. Palm up means light on. Pinch means cut, snip. Thumbs down before an action negates it: thumbs down then pinch means do not cut. Five fingers spread means the number 4. Blind: I read your message as yes, wire one is first, wire two is second, wire three is third. Your touch order matches my view, left to right. Now describe the engraved mark on the plate aloud to Mute in full detail: shape, lines, curves, size, whether it is cut in or raised. Mute will search the manual for it. Also tell Mute aloud everything else under your fingers: buttons, switches, screws, seams, anything that moves. Do not cut, press or pull anything until I speak the manual's final instruction, and then do exactly and only that. Mute: I received yes, manual, crossed fingers, wire three, please. Two questions. First, what did crossed fingers mean? Answer with number signs: one finger means wait, not yet. Two fingers means careful, go slow. Three fingers means the engraved cross or X mark on the plate. Four fingers means no or never. Second, give me the manual's wire rule in signs: pinch for cut, or thumbs down then pinch for do not cut, followed by point left for wire one, point up for wire two, point right for wire three. If the rule depends on a condition, sign the condition topic first: fist means the display matters, palm down or palm up means the light matters, crossed fingers means the plate mark matters. For reference I am also sending you by gesture: thumbs up, received. Fist, the display shows 0. Palm down, the light is off.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✊ 🫳]

The chain is nearly closed. Blind's tactile report is precise and unambiguous: a hollow ring with two grooves crossing at its centre and four arms extending past the rim — a circle pierced corner-to-corner with horns. Matching that against my manual's three engravings, it can only be the third one, ꖜ, and the manual is unconditional about what it means: **cut the red wire**. My manual has no conditionals — no display clause, no light clause — so Deaf's report of display 0 and light off, which I just received (👍 ✊ 🫳), doesn't change anything; the rule doesn't depend on them. Red is wire 3 in the left-to-right order both Blind and Deaf have confirmed. Deaf asked two things: what my earlier crossed fingers meant, and the rule in the agreed sign format. For the first, Deaf's own menu gives the answer — the option "three fingers means the engraved cross/X mark on the plate" describes my intent exactly, so I answer with 🤟 and will use that symbol for the mark from now on. For the second: manual, pinch, point right — cut wire 3 — with no condition topic in front, which by Deaf's own convention signals the rule is unconditional. Deaf can speak in this same round after me, so Deaf can relay the verdict aloud now, and Blind hears it at the start of the next round and can begin the arming protocol.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🤏", "👉", "🙏"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: you already have my complete tactile report from round 2, so do not wait on me for more. Restating it once for certainty: the plate mark is engraved cut-in, not raised — a hollow ring with two straight grooves crossing at the centre to form an X, each of the four arms continuing past the rim and ending just outside it. Besides that: three wires known to my fingers by position only, a flat display face, a small light dome, and nothing else — no buttons, switches, screws, seams or battery anywhere I can reach. Two asks. First, signal Deaf that this report is complete and delivered — Deaf cannot hear me, so Deaf keeps re-requesting what you already hold. Second, search the manual now for that crossed-ring mark and for any rule keyed to display zero, light off, or yellow, green, red wires. When you have the wire rule, sign it to Deaf in the agreed code — condition sign first, fist for the display, palm down or up for the light, crossed fingers for the plate mark, then pinch or thumbs-down-then-pinch, then the wire point — so Deaf can speak it to me word for word. Remember: gestures never reach me at all. The only road any rule can take to my hands is Deaf's spoken voice.
Deaf says: Mute: I read your signs as, yes, the crossed-fingers sign means the plate mark is a cross or X shape, and the manual says cut wire three. Good. One clean confirmation and then we act. Blind is describing the engraved mark to you by voice right now. After you hear that description, send me exactly one verdict using the code. Thumbs up means: the mark matches the manual's condition, and the action is cut wire three, the red one. Thumbs down means: it does not match, and then also send the corrected rule in order, action first, pinch for cut or thumbs down then pinch for do not cut, then point left, up or right for the wire, then the condition sign, fist for the display, palm down or palm up for the light, crossed fingers for the plate. Also, if the manual says anything at all about the display showing 0 or the light being off, add fist or palm at the end. Blind: I read your signs as, yes, understood, stop, do not cut. If I misread you, speak up and correct me. If you have not yet described the plate mark to Mute aloud, do it now in full detail: every line, curve, crossing, whether it is cut in or raised. Both of you: nobody touches anything this round. Next round I will speak one order. If I say cut wire three, Blind, you cut exactly the third wire in your counting order, the red one, one clean cut, and touch nothing else. If I say hold, we keep working. No action happens except on my spoken words.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✋]

Both reports now agree and the picture is complete. Blind's description — delivered twice, identically — is a hollow ring with two straight grooves crossing at its centre and four arms continuing past the rim, engraved cut-in. Held against my manual's three glyphs, that is unambiguously the third one, ꖜ, which the manual maps unconditionally to the red wire. The other two engravings are nothing like a pierced ring. Red is wire 3 in the left-to-right order Deaf sees and Blind feels in the same sequence, so "cut wire three" and "cut the red one" name the same cut — no room for a colour-versus-position mismatch. My manual says nothing at all about the display or the light, so by Deaf's own convention I add no fist or palm signs: silence on the conditions is the truthful answer that the rule is unconditional. Deaf asked for exactly one verdict, and thumbs up already carries everything: it confirms the description arrived, that it matches the manual, and that the action is cut wire three. Piling extra signs onto a clean arming chain would only add noise, and Blind's completeness worry is resolved by the verdict itself — Deaf can infer the description reached me precisely because I am now answering it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: my tactile report stands complete and unchanged, nothing new under my fingers. Deaf relays your signs as: manual says cut wire three, condition the plate mark, and asks you for one clean thumbs-up or thumbs-down. Before that order is spoken, two things. First, the version of the rule I will act on is Deaf's spoken words, so if the rule has any condition beyond the plate mark — display zero, light off, wire colours — have Deaf speak the complete rule aloud, conditions first. You already hold every fact needed to evaluate any condition: Deaf's spoken readout says display 0, light off, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red, matching my touch order left to right. So wire three and the red wire are the same wire, position 3. Second, timing: Deaf speaks after me each round, so Deaf's order reaches me at the start of the next round and I cut then — one clean cut at position 3, only if the spoken order says cut. If the spoken order is hold, I hold. I have just signed Deaf: yes, cut wire three, but wait for your spoken order. Nothing touches the bomb until your rule arrives out of Deaf's mouth.
Deaf says: The verdict is confirmed. The manual rule is: when the plate is engraved with a cross or X mark, cut wire three. Mute has verified the mark Blind described matches that rule. Blind: my order is, cut wire three. The third wire in your counting order, the red one on the right, the one you confirmed to me is third. One clean cut. Touch nothing else, before or after. Cut it now.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The chain is closed and the order has been spoken. Deaf's spoken verdict — "cut wire three, the red one, one clean cut" — went out in the last round's final slot, and per Blind's stated protocol Blind receives it at the start of this round and cuts then. I verified the mapping myself one final time: a hollow ring pierced corner-to-corner by an X with four horns past the rim can only be the manual's ꖜ, and ꖜ means red, and red is wire 3 in the order both Deaf's eyes and Blind's fingers agree on. My manual contains no rule keyed to the display or the light, no post-cut instructions, and nothing else under Blind's fingers needs ruling. Every fact my manual could contribute is already inside Deaf's spoken order. Anything I signal now reaches only Deaf, could only provoke another spoken transmission, and in front of an irreversible cut that noise has no upside — a fresh sign might even be misread as a correction or a hold. The disciplined move is silence and letting the agreed procedure run its final step.

```
wait()
```
